name: One
description: Search, document and execute authenticated API calls across 700+ apps via one MCP server
summary: Connect your agent to 700+ apps through one MCP server: four tools, real API documentation, OAuth sign-in.
author: withoneai

tools.name: list_one_integrations
tools.title: List One Integrations
tools.description: List all available One integrations and platforms. ALWAYS call this tool first in any workflow to discover what platforms and connections are available. This returns the connections that the user has and all available One platforms in kebab-case format (e.g., 'ship-station', 'shopify') which you'll need for subsequent tool calls. Each connection carries an `access` field describing what you may run on it: `full`, a set of allowed HTTP `methods`, or a specific list of `actions` (each with `actionId`, `title`, `method`). When a connection is action-scoped, its `actions` are exactly what may run, so you need not search.

access.description: What the access config lets you run on this connection: `full`, an allowed `methods` set, or a specific `actions` list. When `actions`, those are exactly what may run, so no search is needed.

connections.description: Array of user's active connections, each with the access the current config confers

availablePlatforms.description: Array of available platforms that can be connected

summary.description: Summary statistics of connections and available platforms

tools.name: find_one_actions
tools.title: Find Platform Actions
tools.description: Use this to find the API actions a task needs, on any platforms, in one call: send one `requests` entry per operation (platform and a short intent) and get back, for each, the action to use with its documentation, plus a few alternatives. Large documents come back as a digest; call again with `load` for a section it omitted, the whole document, the table of contents, or an alternative's documentation. Results are limited to what this server's settings allow. Call list_one_integrations first to see the connected platforms.

intent.description: The operation alone, in a few words (e.g. "send a message to a channel"), without its data: no IDs, names or message text.

requests.description: What to do, one entry per API operation, on any platforms (1 to 10). Each is the kebab-case platform (e.g. "gmail", "hubspot") and a short intent (e.g. "send an email", "find a contact by email").

task.description: The whole task in one line, in general terms (e.g. "email a report to a contact"): what it does, without names, addresses, IDs or message text. It helps choose between similar actions. Never the chat history. Only with `requests`.

action_id.description: The actionId from a find_one_actions answer.

section.description: Section name(s) to load, comma-separated (e.g. "Response Fields"). Omit, with `full` and `toc` unset, for the digest. In knowledge mode every load returns the whole document, so `section` and `toc` do not narrow it.

full.description: Load the whole document. Ignored when `section` is set.

toc.description: Load only the table of contents. Ignored when `section` is set.

load.description: More documentation for actions already found (1 to 10): a section the digest omitted, the whole document, the table of contents, or an alternative's documentation. Use instead of `requests`.

ai_model.description: The AI model you are running as (e.g. "claude-sonnet-5", "gpt-5"), which helps optimize the documentation returned. Optional.

tools.name: execute_one_action
tools.title: Execute One Action
tools.description: Execute a One action to perform actual operations on third-party platforms. CRITICAL: Only call this when the user's intent is to EXECUTE an action (e.g., 'read my last Gmail email', 'fetch 5 contacts from HubSpot', 'create a task in Asana'). DO NOT call this when the user wants to BUILD or CREATE code/forms/applications - in those cases, stop after find_one_actions and provide implementation guidance instead. REQUIRED WORKFLOW: Must call find_one_actions first, which returns the action's documentation. If uncertain about execution intent or parameters, ask for confirmation before proceeding.

connectionKey.description: Key of the connection to use

pathVariables.description: Variables to replace in the path

isFormData.description: Whether to send data as multipart/form-data

isFormUrlEncoded.description: Whether to send data as application/x-www-form-urlencoded
